#3644. The 25 Best Movies on Netflix to Watch in November 2026

It can be hard to find the best movies on Netflix. We all understand the struggle of scrolling time—hours lost to wading through all of the Netflix movie options that could instead have been spent, you know, watching something. Or maybe something has been sitting patiently in your queue, waiting for someone to give you a nudge to finally press play. So, like a beacon in the night, here’s a guide to 25 of the best films within Netflix’s huge selection—including everything from landmark films to cult classics to Netflix-original hidden gems—updated monthly as films appear on and leave the platform. Take that, decision fatigue. (And if you want a list of the best shows on Netflix, we’ve got one of those too.)

Director: Colin HigginsGenre: ComedyNotable cast: Jane Fonda, Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton, Dabney Coleman, and Elizabeth WilsonMPA rating: PGRotten Tomatoes: 71%Metacritic: 58

After the passing of Dolly Parton this year, rewatching her in her first film role here can feel bittersweet, but it also proves how she was able to conquer all art forms she tried with seeming ease.

The multihyphenate icon once joked to Vanity Fair about taking the role of Doralee Rhodes, saying, “I thought, Well, if it’s a big success, I can just join in there with Lily [Tomlin] and Jane [Fonda]. And if it’s a big flop, I’ll just blame it on them ’cause nobody thinks about me being a movie star.” Parton would also get her first Oscar nomination and two Grammys for the title track, but the comedy gold of this trio taking on their sexist, egotistical, lying, hypocritical bigot boss remains a classic.

Director: James GrayGenre: Space DramaNotable cast: Brad Pitt, Tommy Lee Jones, Ruth Negga, Liv Tyler, Donald Sutherland, John Ortiz, and Natasha LyonneMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 83%Metacritic: 80

As director James Gray prepares to storm the awards season with Paper Tiger—a return to the crime genre that put him on the map—it’s maybe time to reassess his misunderstood and mishandled space elegy Ad Astra. It’s not your typical space exploration adventure, but something much more personal. Starring Brad Pitt as an astronaut who ventures to the depths of our solar system to recover his father (Tommy Lee Jones) after a failed mission, Ad Astra is a more soulful and introspective space film than most audiences were expecting. It didn’t help that post Disney merger, Fox whimpered the film into theatres. “But what has long distinguished Gray, and what rings true in even this [film], his grandest and in some ways most complex movie, is that his movies peer inward, not outward—toward longing, frustration, uncertainty, and rattled expectations, rather than toward resolution,” praised Vanity Fair about what makes Gray’s film so special.

Director: Ridley ScottGenre: HorrorNotable cast: Sigourney Weaver, Tom Skerritt, John Hurt, Ian Holm, Veronica Cartwright, Yaphet Kotto, and Harry Dean StantonMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 89

As the franchise spins its ever divisive sequels and now television shows, it all goes back to the sheer paralyzing terror of Ridley Scott’s original Alien. It’s maybe Jaws’ only rival for the title of greatest monster movie of all time, following the spaceship Nostromo as its crew is besieged by a vicious space creature that picks each member off one by one–eventually meeting its match in Sigourney Weaver’s beloved Ellen Ripley. The film’s influential, Giger-inspired aesthetic arguably remains Scott’s biggest visual calling card and one of the high-water marks for his career, which the Academy will finally recognize this year when he receives his honorary Oscar.

Director: Mati DiopGenre: DramaNotable cast: Mame Bineta Sane, Amadou Mbow, and Ibrahima TraoréMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 96%Metacritic: 85

Achingly romantic and fiercely original, Atlantics is a shape-shifting ghost story of sorts that defies simple categorization. Mati Diop’s first feature follows a young woman set to marry a man she does not love, while her lover flees their native Senegal by sea in search of work. Overnight, spirits begin to possess the townsfolk, seeking revenge against an exploitative corporation. Never less than captivating, the film features unforgettable visuals and an arresting blending of themes that make for one of the most daring Netflix originals—and signal Diop as one of the major breakthrough directors of the past decade.

Director: Paul FeigGenre: ComedyNotable cast: Kristen Wiig, Maya Rudolph, Melissa McCarthy, Rose Byrne, Chris O’Dowd, Ellie Kemper, Wendi McLendon-Covey, Jon Hamm, and Jill ClayburghMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 89%Metacritic: 75

Though Vanity Fair once posited that Bridesmaids was the best comedy of 2011 (amidst stiff competition like Crazy, Stupid, Love), by now we can safely call it the best and funniest comedy of that decade. Kristen Wiig plays a depressed woman whose best friend (Maya Rudolph) gets engaged, kicking off a slow-motion meltdown. Melissa McCarthy got an Oscar nomination as an abrasive but tough-loving puppy-stealer, and an underrated Rose Byrne should have been nominated alongside her as Wiig’s rival, who masks her own insecurities with judgment. Its unforgettable sequences come relentlessly–from Jon Hamm’s sexual lunacy to the notorious food poisoning sequence to a colonial woman churning butter on the wing of an airplane–and it’s only gotten funnier in recent years when we have been served too few comedies.

Director: Kirsten JohnsonGenre: DocumentaryMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 99%Metacritic: 89

Kirsten Johnson is always breaking the boundaries of what we think a documentary can be—never more so than in her deeply moving yet not-depressing tribute to her father on the eve of his death. Between candid interviews with her father, Dick, Johnson stages his death in various, surreally funny scenarios, such as a fall down the stairs or being struck by a rogue air conditioner. The director told Vanity Fair that making the film was an act of coping with her beloved parent’s dementia: “How can my father and I together confront the fact that he, who is irreplaceable, will disappear?” The effect is whimsical, profound, and restorative, making for the wildest study of love and loss in Netflix’s vast stable.

Director: Takashi YamazakiGenre: ActionNotable cast: Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Yuki Yamada, Munetaka Aoki, Hidetaka Yoshioka, and Sakura AndoMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 99%Metacritic: 81

We called its newly arriving sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero, one of the most anticipated films of the fall season, and for good reason. Godzilla Minus One was a surprise stateside box office success in 2023, resulting in a wholly deserved visual-effects Oscar (the first for a non-English-language film). The franchise has had many different takes over the years, but Takashi Yamazaki’s telling of the monster tale is the perfect pairing of large-scale bravura visuals and grounded human emotion. This revamp centers around the end of WW II, using the aftereffects of war to tell a human story of survivor’s guilt amidst all the destruction caused by the world’s most iconic movie monster.

Director: Alice RohrwacherGenre: DramaNotable cast: Adriano Tardiolo, Sergi López, and Alba RohrwacherMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 87

Director Alice Rohrwacher earned a legion of new fans from 2023’s Josh O’Conner–led La Chimera—but prior to that masterpiece, she made another with this idiosyncratic fable. Another foray into symbolic magical realism, the story of frozen-in-time sweetheart farmhand Lazzaro is used by Rohwacher to weave a magical examination of class and exploitation. Around its midpoint, the film takes a daring leap that recontextualizes everything we have seen as more than meets the eye, setting the tender Lazzaro on a course for tragedy to come. It’s one of Rohrwacher’s bespoke visual wonders that seem to commune with some kind of cinematic deity, casting a spell that lingers long after viewing.

Director: Michael MannGenre: CrimeNotable cast: [Deep breath] Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Val Kilmer, Tom Sizemore, Amy Brenneman, Natalie Portman, Ashley Judd, Dennis Haysbert, Mykelti Williamson, Jon Voight, Wes Studi, and at least a dozen moreMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 84%Metacritic: 76

Audiences were initially slightly underwhelmed by Heat in 1995—while they were promised a fireworks showdown between Al Pacino and Robert De Niro for the first time onscreen, director Michael Mann gave them something more introspective and psychological. Heat is instead something of an existential heist epic that took a few years for folks to really appreciate. Now considered Mann’s defining masterpiece, the film has earned a devoted, die-hard cult following. Thirty years on, this crime thriller is finally appreciated for being more than an action film—its sensory precision is as captivating as its brooding, masculine psychology.

Director: Azazel JacobsGenre: DramaNotable cast: Carrie Coon, Natasha Lyonne, Elizabeth Olsen, Jovan Adepo, and Jay O. SandersMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 98%Metacritic: 83

Carrie Coon, Natasha Lyonne, and Elizabeth Olsen give three revelatory performances as diametrically opposed estranged siblings—the dictator, the hippie, and the burnout, respectively. They cram together in a tiny New York City apartment as they await the death of their father. They battle over groceries, monologue about the Grateful Dead, and try (and fail) to keep their many past resentments at bay. Sure, His Three Daughters is at times a painful watch, brimming with claustrophobic tension and biting wit. But writer-director Azazel Jacobs gives this chamber piece on death and family a light touch, lifting it off into something unexpected in its emotional depth and making for one of 2024’s best films.

Director: Brett HaleyGenre: RomanceNotable cast: Blythe Danner, Sam Elliott, Martin Starr, June Squibb, Mary Kay Place, Rhea Perlman, and Malin AkermanMPA rating: PG-13Rotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 75

Featuring one of the standout performances of Blythe Danner’s career, I’ll See You in My Dreams was a bittersweet, small-scale hit in 2015. Danner stars as a widowed woman who gets a new lease on life when she tiptoes back into dating, resulting in a love affair with a dashing Sam Elliott. It’s a delicate and memorable tale of aging—not only due to Danner’s incredible performance, but also because of its surprising musical edge (Danner sings again onscreen) and delightful trio of actors as Danner’s hilarious friends: June Squibb, Mary Kay Place, and Rhea Perlman. Elliott is also a remarkable romantic star here, and this film (paired with another strong performance in Grandma the same year) helped kick off a career resurgence for the star that culminated in his first Oscar nomination in 2019 for A Star Is Born.

Director: Martin ScorseseGenre: CrimeNotable cast: Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci, Harvey Keitel, Bobby Cannavale, Ray Romano, Stephen Graham, Jesse Plemons, Jack Huston, Marin Ireland, and Anna PaquinMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 95%Metacritic: 94

Martin Scorsese’s epic fable on legacy, loyalty, and unions follows the life of Mob hit man Frank Sheeran, played by Robert De Niro. As Vanity Fair put it, “There’s something crucial about sitting with the same actors for so long. It communicates the weight and ravages of time more keenly than if the actors had been swapped out halfway through.” Much was made of the de-aging visual effects that allowed De Niro to play the character at all stages of Sheeran’s life, as was about Netflix’s refusal to play ball with the theater chains for the film’s limited theatrical release. Now that all that dust has settled, what remains is one of the defining masterpieces of this late stage of Scorsese’s career, one with a lot to say about where to place your loyalties and priorities in life.

Director: David LeanGenre: Epic dramaNotable cast: Peter O’Toole, Omar Sharif, Alec Guinness, Anthony Quinn, Jack Hawkins, Claude Rains, and José FerrerMPA rating: PGRotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 100

Netflix is not prone to offering many films from before the 1990s, so when a landmark work is on the platform, attention must be paid. David Lean’s masterpiece is widely beloved for good reason: In telling of the WW I exploits of T.E. Lawrence, Lean crafted a vivid cinematic language that would be emulated by the best directors for generations to come. Indelibly tied to the legacy of its star, Peter O’Toole, the film remains the gold standard for war epics and biopics about complicated historical figures alike. Though the film has often been trimmed and abbreviated in various releases over its lifetime, Netflix is streaming the “restored version,” which offers the film in full three-hour-and-47-minute splendor—the trick is not minding that it’s long!

Director: Rian JohnsonGenre: Sci-fiNotable cast: Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Bruce Willis, Emily Blunt, Jeff Daniels, Paul Dano, Garret Dillahunt, Noah Segan, and Piper PeraboMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 93%Metacritic: 84

Rian Johnson may have spent the last decade in the realm of multiple franchises, between Benoit Blanc and Star Wars, but his first hit came with 2012’s heady sci-fi film Looper. The film casts Joseph Gordon-Levitt as a futuristic assassin tasked with killing his older self (played to career-topping brilliance by Bruce Willis) via time travel. As you might expect, nothing goes to plan. But this is just the beginning of Johnson’s unexpected twists, including an incredible performance from Emily Blunt that showed off for the first time her ability to balance action-star bravado with emotionally affecting pathos. Even after Johnson’s head-spinning, big-budget success, this is maybe the biggest benchmark for his ability to deliver something that’s several steps ahead of the audience.

Director: Todd HaynesGenre: DramaNotable cast: Natalie Portman, Julianne Moore, Charles MeltonMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 86

Todd Haynes’s darkly comedic, sleazy satire stars Natalie Portman as an actor who becomes obsessed with the real-life figure she is about to play: a former teacher (Julianne Moore) who became a tabloid fixture for her sexual relationship with a teenage student (Charles Melton). As much as the film skewers tabloid culture (it’s loosely inspired by Mary Kay Letourneau), it’s also a darkly comedic look at performance and the lies we tell ourselves. In calling it one of the best films of 2023, Vanity Fair wrote, “May December could probably be endlessly unpacked, so varied are its tones and textures and piercing insights.”

Director: Christopher NolanGenre: Noir thrillerNotable cast: Guy Pearce, Carrie-Anne Moss, Joe Pantoliano, Stephen Tobolowsky, and Harriet Sansom HarrisMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 94%Metacritic: 83

Who? Christopher Nolan? Oh yeah, heard of him! As the world-adored director takes audiences back to early civilization this summer with The Odyssey, Netflix takes you back to his early career with the neo-noir dazzler Memento. His sophomore feature, the film made major waves by telling its grimy vigilante tale from the beginning and the end, working both backward and forward until it all meets in the middle for a shocking twist. The creative editing trick put Nolan’s name on the map, propelling him from indie darling to must-have director for the studios, and the rest is history. If you haven’t caught up to the film, it’s proof that Nolan has always been a master of mixing up timelines in order to blow our minds.

Director: Barry JenkinsGenre: DramaNotable cast: Mahershala Ali, Trevante Rhodes, Naomie Harris, André Holland, Ashton Sanders, Jharrel Jerome, and Janelle MonáeMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 98%Metacritic: 99

Celebrating its 10th anniversary this year, Barry Jenkins’s landmark Black queer drama Moonlight follows the coming-of-age and queer acceptance of Chiron over three chapters of his life. Through childhood, teen years, and early adulthood, we see Chiron taken under the wing of a drug dealer (an immaculate and Oscar-winning Mahershala Ali) and face the addiction battles of his mother (Naomie Harris) and the inner demons of masculinity and homosexuality. “Jenkins has made a breathtaking film, one with political urgency and a deep, compassionate humanity,” said Vanity Fair in its review upon the film’s festival debut, “Moonlight is timely and timeless, a study in limits that casts its gaze up toward something transcendent.” While we remember the fraught circumstances of its best picture win at the Academy Awards, the film remains one of the key masterpieces of this generation of filmmakers.

Director: Paul Thomas AndersonGenre: RomanceNotable cast: Daniel Day-Lewis, Vicky Krieps, Lesley Manville, and Harriet Sansom HarrisMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 90Now that Paul Thomas Anderson has won his Oscar(s) with last year’s One Battle After Another, we can rest easy knowing that his eccentric filmography has finally been recognized. But his most atypical film is perhaps 2017’s Phantom Thread, a romance that’s swoony and caustic in equal measure. Demanding diva couturier Reynolds Woodcock (Daniel Day-Lewis, in what was then supposed to be his final performance) falls for straight-shooting waitress Alma (Vicky Krieps, in her breakout role), resulting in a marriage that by turns fuels Reynolds’s creative inspiration and has them hilariously at each other’s throats. In true PTA fashion, any tenderness is never without its sharp corners, but it’s nevertheless his most sumptuous movie.

Director: Jane CampionGenre: DramaNotable cast: Benedict Cumberbatch, Kirsten Dunst, Jesse Plemons, Kodi Smit-McPhee, Thomasin McKenzie, Keith Carradine, and Frances ConroyMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 94%Metacritic: 89

Jane Campion’s big-screen return earned high praise for its psychologically intense study of masculinity in the American West. It’s never quite the movie you expect: In calling it one of 2021’s best films, Vanity Fair critic Richard Lawson said this “stately and mysterious film isn’t quite a character-study drama, not quite a thriller, and not really a Western. It is an elusive and mesmerizing thing unto itself.” An all-consuming visual experience, The Power of the Dog features top-to-bottom outstanding performances from its cast, including Benedict Cumberbatch as one of the most terrifying movie villains in recent memory. It’s not just one of the best movies on Netflix right now; it’s one of the best movies ever.

Director: Tamara JenkinsGenre: ComedyNotable cast: Paul Giamatti, Kathryn Hahn, Molly Shannon, John Carroll Lynch, Kayli Carter, and Denis O’HareMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 94%Metacritic: 83

In one of Netflix’s best movies and most overlooked masterworks, Kathryn Hahn and Paul Giamatti star as an infertile New York City couple who, after several unsuccessful attempts at fertility treatment, consider surrogacy with their wayward niece (Kayli Carter). It’s only the third entry in writer-director Tamara Jenkins’s (flawless) filmography, but it’s maybe the best showcase of her bittersweet comic pathos yet: There’s nude ranting, people shoving their feet in their mouths, and bits about overly specific lox portions. If the film’s final shot doesn’t heal whatever ails you, please consult your doctor. All that, plus a powder keg, career-best performance from Hahn–before she would become a household name with her MCU debut as Agatha in WandaVision–makes this essential viewing.

Director: Alfred HitchcockGenre: ThrillerNotable cast: Anthony Perkins, Janet Leigh, Vera MilesMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 97%Metacritic: 97

Cue the sharp violin strings because it’s Hitchcock-tober! This notorious game-changing thriller that made an entire generation afraid to go into the shower remains Hitchcock’s most iconic movie for a reason. It practically invented the plot twist, and it has two of them that movies have been borrowing from since. However, Psycho still reigns supreme for its narrative nerve and pervy ability to shock, led by Anthony Perkins’s tetchy, slowly unnerving performance as the killer, Norman Bates. Like the aforementioned Lawrence of Arabia, Psycho is currently one of the rare films from before the 1990s available on Netflix, so for folks looking more for film history (whether for a rewatch or a first watch), now is the time.

Director: Rob ReinerGenre: Coming-of-age dramaNotable cast: Wil Wheaton, River Phoenix, Corey Feldman, Jerry O’Connell, Kiefer Sutherland, and Richard DreyfussMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 89%Metacritic: 76

After Rob Reiner’s tragic death, the love for his greatest cultural touchstones was reignited. Though he gave us such beloved films as When Harry Met Sally…, Misery, and The Princess Bride, many would still anoint Stand by Me as his career peak—not for nothing, Vanity Fair has called it the best Stephen King movie. Based on King’s novella The Body, it follows a group of young friends who go in search of a dead body in the wilderness, gently touching on themes of death and masculinity that bruise us in much the same way that the experience does its young heroes. Forty years on, it’s still an enduring classic about the trials of growing up—and for good reason.

Director: Yance FordGenre: DocumentaryMPA rating: UnratedRotten Tomatoes: 100%Metacritic: 86

Ford tackles his own family history and the injustice of the legal system with this nonfiction stunner, a recounting of his brother’s 1992 murder and how the killer went free. Where other documentaries navel-gaze at the details of a murder, Strong Island is more interested in the aftermath of the crime—how his brother’s killer going free shaped both his identity and his family’s. Ford approaches such personal subject matter with a sober and unflinching formal rigor, including some audacious moments where he directly addresses the camera. The result is a film that’s something of an antidote to the rise of the exploitative true crime documentary, a deeply intimate and searingly introspective portrait of a still-grieving family denied justice.

Director: Sarah PolleyGenre: DramaNotable cast: Michelle Williams, Seth Rogen, Luke Kirby, and Sarah SilvermanMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 79%Metacritic: 68

Sarah Polley is one of the greatest living multihyphenates (she’s acted and written books with equal brilliance!), but her directorial output has proven to be the most singular part of her career. Between giving Julie Christie a career resurgence with Away From Her and winning an Oscar for Women Talking, Polley made a more divisive film in the infidelity character study Take This Waltz. The sexy, frankly observed film stars Michelle Williams as a young woman who, despite her idyllic life, finds herself surprisingly adrift as she approaches 30, leading her to drift away from her all-too-perfect husband, played by Seth Rogen (before he would bring Polley out of acting retirement for The Studio). The movie makes some uncomfortable, perhaps because it’s unflinchingly honest (and nonjudgmental) about the displacement we can feel at a certain stage of our life.

Director: Todd FieldGenre: DramaNotable cast: Cate Blanchett, Nina Hoss, Noémie Merlant, Adam Gopnik, and Mark StrongMPA rating: RRotten Tomatoes: 91%Metacritic: 93

After a 16-year absence, director Todd Field returned with Tár, a story of ego and disgrace for a fallen conductor, played with towering conviction by (a maybe career best) Cate Blanchett. “Field’s film is enormous, contemplating the end of idolism in all its loss and revolution,” raved Vanity Fair. “Tár bracingly responds to the dawning of a new era and reintroduces the world to a filmmaker who seems only better for having taken some time, a very long time indeed, to listen and to learn.” What’s immediately apparent is the precision with which Field takes to this dissection of a post-#MeToo downfall of a powerful person who has done bad things (with the film told entirely from their myopic perspective), but a rewatch reveals it’s also ruefully funny as well.

#3643. GOG Wants To Bring Back Physical PC Games, But There’s A Catch

While PlayStation 5 console owners are preparing for a discless future, PC gamers have been living in all-digital world for decades now. The advent of Steam and cheaper broadband internet helped end physical PC game sales in the early 2000s, but GOG is dreaming up a future where these games can thrive once again--if it can get past a few obstacles that stand in its way.

Speaking to GamesRadar, Marcin Paczynski, GOG's senior business development and partnerships manager, laid out a dream scenario in which a consumer can browse GOG, select a game, and have a physical copy delivered to their home. "Ideally, my dream would be to be able to buy physical versions of those games on GOG," Paczynski said. "You go to your shelf on GOG, you click on the game that you would like to receive a physical copy of, you order it, and it gets to you. That would be a perfect scenario."

While that sounds ideal, it's easier said than done, as Paczynski noted that selling physical goods is a logistical challenge when compared to running a digital storefront. Physical media requires organizing storage, delivery, and additional publisher approvals, but Paczynski hopes to see it realized one day.

It's worth noting that the GOG Preservation Program did recently create high-resolution scans for five classic games--Myst, Descent, Hitman: Codename 47, Star Trek: 25th Anniversary, and Armikrog--and turned them into 3D models that you can view on your PC--as well as printable files for anyone looking for a papercraft project. It's similar to the work done by another site, Big Box Collection, which offers a far larger library of classic PC boxes to admire in 3D.

GOG isn't the only company nostalgic for the big boxes of a bygone era; several sites have popped up in recent years to offer curated collections of physical PC and console games. From Limited Run Games to Special Reserve Games, there's still an appetite for owning something with a tangible quality.

#3642. Borderlands Franchise Hits 100 Million Sales As Gearbox Hints At What’s Next

The Borderlands franchise has reached a new sales milestone, as developer Gearbox Software announced that Borderlands 4 had pushed the series over the 100 million units sold mark. Celebrating the achievement, the studio also took time to reveal what's next for Borderlands 4 as it enters its second year, as well as plans it's busy cooking up for the IP.

"We just wrapped our Year 1 roadmap, and the team is cooking hard on more Borderlands 4 content for next year," Gearbox wrote in a blog post, adding that weekly activity refreshes and Community Challenges will continue in the game. So what's next for Borderlands? Gearbox says that it's "a bigger look at the franchise as a whole," and it's also listening to fans to gauge which characters they want to spend more time with.

Don't expect Gearbox to drop a Borderlands 5 announcement anytime soon, as the developer said it needs time and space to work on future projects. "Big plans take time, and we need some room to work. You can trust that we’ll talk more when the time is right," Gearbox added. Thirteen months ago, Gearbox Software boss Randy Pitchford had predicted that Borderlands 4 would continue to sell millions of copies and would help the franchise cross the 100 million units sold line eventually. "We will break 100 million units with this launch, easily, all in, with the franchise," Pitchford said at the time.

To put that in perspective, the Borderlands franchise had sold 94 million units through August 2025, meaning Borderlands 4 would move at least 6 million copies. Historically, Borderlands 2 is the franchise's top seller, with 31 million units sold, while Borderlands 3 is second with 23 million sales to date. It's worth noting that these games have also gone on sale regularly--with Borderlands 3 once being sold for just $3 on PC via Steam--and Borderlands 4 has also received a few discounts since launch. Gearbox and publisher Take-Two Interactive haven't revealed sales figures for Borderlands 4 yet, so it's hard to know where it currently fits on the Borderlands sales chart.

The game didn't have a smooth launch either, as various technical hurdles required multiple rounds of patching, and the oft-delayed Switch 2 edition was eventually paused so that Gearbox could focus on the PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S editions of the game.

#3641. Alexa and Carlos PenaVega ‘Hopeful’ About Welcoming Baby After Stillbirth

Alexa PenaVega and Carlos PenaVega are open to welcoming another baby two years after their daughter Indy was stillborn.

“We talk about … having one last baby, if we can,” Carlos, 37, wrote in the afterword of the couple’s Joy Isn’t Canceled: What Grief Taught Us About Pain, Peace, and Purpose memoir. “Those conversations feel hopeful in a way I didn’t think they ever would.”

Alexa, 38, and Carlos revealed in April 2024 that her pregnancy with their fourth child ended in a stillbirth. (The couple, who have been married since 2014, also share sons Ocean and Kingston, as well as daughter Rio.)

Alexa’s pregnancy with Indy was plagued by a number of complications, including blood loss, that required multiple hospitalizations. In Joy Isn’t Canceled, Alexa and Carlos open up about finding solace in their faith while grieving Indy’s death.

“Grief changed me,” Carlos acknowledged in the epilogue. “I had to stop pretending everything was OK when it wasn’t. I had to learn how to say what I was really thinking and feeling, even when it scared me. That changed me, and it changed our marriage too.”

The Spy Kids actress and the Big Time Rush musician have continued to honor Indy’s memory in the years since her death.

“Indy’s life is so full. She may be in heaven, but, like, she is so full,” Alexa recalled on the “Dear Future Husband” podcast in August. I didn’t grow up thinking about death, you know, ‘cause it’s scary. Death has lost its sting. We have felt the valley, and I think we feared the valley so much because everyone told us to fear the valley, but in the valley with God, there are diamonds.”

She continued at the time, “The valley is loaded with rubies and gold and gems and the things that everyone is so afraid to go get, you know, and here we are, like, swimming in luxury in the worst time of our lives because He was just there for us.”

Alexa further revealed how Indy’s loss strengthened her marriage.

“When her loss happened, it was still a big blow, but [God’s] peace was so evident and so all over our lives, and the way he used her life to ignite our family,” Alexa noted. “I hear about these couples who end up breaking up after the loss of a child and it hurts my heart so much because, for us, it ignited us. It was, like, the fan to the flame that [made us] so much more intentional with each other. Walls were broken.”

Joy Isn’t Canceled: What Grief Taught Us About Pain, Peace and Purpose is out now.

#3640. Remedy’s Big Bet On Control Resonant Appears To Be Paying Off

Following the September release of Control Resonant, business is boomin' for developer Remedy Entertainment. The studio reported that its third-quarter revenue surged 226% to €39.6 million / $44.3 million after the game's release, following the financial review period on October 15, a feat CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon called "a defining milestone" for Remedy.

In terms of operating profit, Remedy said it made €0.6 million / $670,794, and while that may not sound like much, it's still better than the €16.4 million / $18.3 million loss the studio posted in the same quarter last year. Control Resonant has sold over 1 million units, making it Remedy's fastest-selling title to date, with most sales coming from the US. The game has also been popular in the US and the UK, and Remedy says that half of the players were new to the franchise.

"Reaching new players was a key goal for this game, and these early results indicate a growing audience for the franchise and for Remedy," Gaudechon said, adding that the developer is looking to get the game into the hands of more people. Control Resonant's predecessor, Control, also saw increased sales, and that financial runway will help Remedy as it continues working on other projects, like its Max Payne 1 & 2 remake. Gaudechon also noted that Control Resonant is currently on 2.4 million wishlists, which could provide a "substantial potential audience" for the future.

"Excellent player reviews, penetration in all our target markets and a substantial outstanding wishlist base give a solid foundation for the game’s longer-term sales potential, supported by both organic visibility as well as our targeted marketing activities," said Gaudechon. As for the other games in the Remedy catalog, Gaudechon said that most people are playing FBC: Firebreak through subscription services like Game Pass or PlayStation Plus, and in its second year, it is making less money. The Alan Wake franchise had a quieter quarter, but the Alan Wake 2 capitalized development costs were fully depreciated during Q3.

For more on Control Resonant, read up on how different it is from its predecessor, why you have to watch out for scary buses, and the cool little details lurking in the background.

Since Patrick Stewart's death became public knowledge nearly a week ago, many across social media have been taking the time to honor the late actor. Also, a number celebrities have been honoring Stewart, including more than a few of his Star Trek cohorts. On that note, John de Lancie is now adding his voice to the many who've been sharing their memories of the Jean-Luc Picard portrayer. The beloved Q actor paid a fitting tribute to his former co-star and dropped the perfect reference tied to Picard and Q's past tussles.

While he wasn't a main character, John de Lancie's Q became one of Star Trek: The Next Generation's most memorable foes. After many adventures over the years, including Picard, De Lancie posted the following message about Stewart on Facebook:

For forty years, Q has been a thorn in Jean-Luc Picard’s side. And what a pleasure it has been to be that thorn. Patrick Stewart was a wonderful actor. He brought intelligence and depth to every role he played. It was a privilege to have worked with him. The universe is a little smaller and a little less bright today with his passing. Goodbye, Patrick. You touched so many. See you out there, Mon Capitaine.

That "mon Capitaine" brought a tear to my eye when I read it, and reminded me of some of my favorite TNG episodes. While Q and Picard's relationship ran hot and cold, I could always sense that it was always love coming from the former's end. Of course, he was certainly a jerk, putting Picard through some wtf-worthy scenarios, but I always appreciated that there was some mutual love between them at the end of Picard's second season.

I'm A Star Trek Fan, But I'd Never Heard This Cool Story About Patrick Stewart Showing Up On Jeremy Clarkson's Set

For those who haven't streamed Picard Season 2 with a Paramount+ subscription, the storyline ends with Picard's realization that Q has constructed the entire scenario he's put them through in order to help him overcome past trauma. Q then reveals to Picard that he is dying, and the two share a hug before Q sets the timeline right again.

It was emotional for me, even if it was potentially retconned when Picard Season 3 had Q return in a post-credits scene. Fans have, however, theorized that everything from the Q species exists outside of time. Therefore, his death doesn't have to be linear.

Personally, I think Q is not above faking his own death just for the thrill of pulling one over on Picard. The fact of the matter is, we'll likely never know now that Patrick Stewart is gone, though I'm sure he won't be the last to play Picard. Star Trek hasn't been afraid to recast iconic characters, though I think it'll be a challenge for someone to follow in Stewart's footsteps and play the role.

Patrick Stewart's death comes amid the celebration of Star Trek's 60th anniversary, which has been rife with bad news. As far as the franchise itself goes, there is a movie in development, but no TV shows are actively in the works as far as the general public knows. Stewart's passing certainly feels like a gut punch to the fandom and the former actors, many of whom held out hope for positive news before the year's end.

Tributes continue to pour in for Patrick Stewart, and I'm continuing to love every eulogy and story that is shared. Both Star Trek: The Next Generation and Picard are available to stream on Paramount+, so anyone who is missing the great Captain should head over there and watch some classic episodes.

#3638. South Of Midnight Director Says He Would Not Have Funded The Game

Xbox funded and published 2025's South of Midnight, a highly acclaimed action-adventure game set in the American Deep South. The game's creative director, David Sears, said he believes South of Midnight is a "generational" game that he hopes people discover and play for a long time and one that he thought would help elevate the "prestige" of Xbox.

At the same time, Sears said he wasn't sure Microsoft's spending spree under the previous leaders Phil Spencer and Sarah Bond--which is how Sears' studio Compulsion got the funding to make South of Midnight--was going to work out long term.

"I literally told people, I was like, 'Yeah, wow, this could be terrible.' Because somebody is going to say, someday, 'The money tap ... we're closing those floodgates.' And that's going to have really traumatic results downstream," he told Ben Hanson on MinnMax.

Microsoft spent billions and billions of dollars to buy studios and franchises to help get Xbox Game Pass off the ground. The bet did not work out, and now Spencer and Bond are out. The new Xbox CEO is Asha Sharma, and one of her first moves was to cut costs dramatically with layoffs, studio divestures--including Compulsion--and game cancellations. Sharma also talked about how Game Pass needs to evolve into something that's "more enticing to a broader range of customers.”

Asked directly if he had been in control of the Xbox funding at the time, would Sears have stopped writing checks for games like South of Midnight? "Yeah, probably," he answered (via Kotaku).

"I wanted to make it. No doubt. Obviously. Because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else’s money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah. Because I’m not completely selfless. It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable," Sears said.

A lot of people said Microsoft's spending on Xbox Game Pass was unsustainable and ultimately going to lead to pain and turmoil. Raphael Colantonio, the co-founder of Arkane, said Game Pass is unsustainable and "increasingly damaging" to the industry. Game Pass has been propped up by Microsoft's "infinite money," Colantonio said.

Raccoon Logic studio head Alex Hutchinson spoke out about Game Pass devaluing games earlier this year after his game Revenge of the Savage Planet was a day-one title on Xbox Game Pass. Conversely, Rebellion touted the launch of Atomfall on Game Pass as a huge success for the company.

With Microsoft's big bets not panning out in the way the company envisioned, the Xbox business struggled, and the ensuing Xbox "reset" has been painful for the people, teams, and fans of Xbox. Sears said hindsight is 20/20, but he always had a feeling that things just weren't right and that the bottom could fall out one day in terms of Xbox's spending spree.

"Of course it was going to have a 'shocking' outcome. It’s easy to dissect it now. But at the time ... I would talk to other directors and [they’d] be like, 'How is this happening? How did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like ... 'For now,'" he said. "And there’s always a night when Rome burns. I didn’t know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Sears went on to say the Microsoft of today is "much more humane" than the company was in the '90s and 2000s, something he said is "remarkable and commendable."

Sears said it's a good thing that Microsoft is allowing studios it wants to let go of get spun out instead of shutting them down outright. Compulsion, for its part, was among the studios that got spun out, and is now operating independently and seeking new projects and funding sources.

South of Midnight originally launched for Xbox and PC in April 2025, later coming to PS5 and Switch 2 in March 2026. Now that Compulsion is independent, buying the game supports the studio directly, and not Xbox.

Throughout all of the downturns at Xbox, Microsoft continues to make gigantic sums of money, in part because Xbox represents just a tiny sliver of the company's overall business. For the latest quarter, Microsoft made $92.3 billion in revenue (up 19%) and a profit of $36.6 billion (up 32%). Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has praised Sharma for gutting the Xbox business so heavily.

#3637. Country Singer Nicole Taylor Dead at 35 After Terminal Breast Cancer Diagnosis

Nicole Taylor, a member of the country music trio Taylor Red, has died after a battle with breast cancer. She was 35.

Nicole’s triplet sisters, Nika and Natalie Taylor, announced her death in a video shared via TikTok and Instagram on Monday, November 2.

“We’re heartbroken to announce the passing of our sister Nicole Taylor,” Nika said. “We honestly thought she’d be healed here on Earth, but now she’s healed in heaven.”

The sisters revealed that Nicole was diagnosed with stage III breast cancer in 2022.

“It was an aggressive type. In her words, when she first found out, was, ‘God’s gonna use this for his glory,’” Natalie said.

Nika continued, “She fought it fearlessly, and she said, ‘We’re not going to live in dread during all of this.’ And she even did CrossFit while she was doing her chemo treatments. She responded well to treatments, and she was declared evidence without disease.”

Nicole’s health then took a turn for the worse, and her illness progressed to stage IV.

“She tried not to live in fear, remained really hopeful. She traveled, she tried to live life, she worked really hard, she tried to have fun,” Natalie said.

Nine months later, Nicole was told she had “around three months” to live.

“And if the treatments worked, they didn’t know how long after that,” Nika explained, while Natalie recalled their sister telling the doctor, “Everybody’s going to face judgment, and I’m ready to.”

The sisters then shared a clip of Nicole in her 20s discussing her faith, which she said helped her through her cancer battle.

“She lived around a year after that prognosis, and during the time of the more extreme diagnosis, we felt led to not live in fear and claim healing, and God encouraged us in so many ways,” Natalie said.

Nika concluded, “He was with us and Nicole before her passing. She said she had so much peace, and we’re really thankful for that. We are still shocked and didn’t think this would happen, but we know she’s not suffering anymore, and we have God’s promise of ultimate healing.”

In a YouTube video on Monday, Nika and Natalie got emotional as they shared that Nicole’s diagnosis came as a “big shock.”

“We’re still processing everything,” Natalie said. “This, honestly, feels really hard to talk about, but we’re going to do our best to share her story.”

Taylor Red formed in 2010 and went viral on TikTok during the COVID-19 pandemic for their comedy skits and musical challenges. They are best known for their tracks “Country Money” and “Rent Free.”

#3636. Heidi Klum Shocks In Severed Hand Halloween Costume

Heidi Klum has done it again. The Project Runway host exceeded all our Halloween expectations by transforming herself into a giant, severed human hand nearly two meters tall for the latest edition of her annual party, held Saturday night in New York City. The costume, which required hours of work by her makeup and prop team, left no detail to chance: hyper-realistic veins modeled after her own anatomy, wrinkles, red-painted nails, and an exxagerated version of the rings she typically wears.

“Mike [Marino, from the special effects team ProRenFX] has all of these scans of my body, so he was able to use those to create an exact replica of my hand,” Klum explained to Vogue. “We wanted everything to be as realistic as possible—the anatomy, the veins, the muscles, all the little details that make a hand look like a real hand.”

The costume’s structure used the model's legs to form two of the fingers, while her right arm provided mobility for the thumb. Only her eyes and mouth were visible amid the bloody wounds on her palm, from which—to top off the gruesomeness of it all—Heidi Klum would occasionally spit out the fake blood that a team of assistants injected into her mouth. The most macabre part was at the wrist, where a horrific gash exposed a jumble of blood, bones, and torn flesh.

Heidi Klum (L) recieves an injection of fake blood to augment her 2026 Halloween costume.

Other guests at Klum's party included Kyle MacLachlan, who arrived dressed as his character from The Flintstones; Neil Patrick Harris and his husband David Burtka, dressed as the girls from The Shining; and Heidi Klum and Flavio Briatore's daughter, Leni Klum.

Before making her grand entrance, the host had built up anticipation on social media by posting clues about this year’s costume, such as a photo of her real hand that showed her wedding ring alongside the small tattoo of husband Tom Kaulitz's name. It, too, was part of her Halloween costume. “Nothing was overlooked! I love that Mike pays attention to things that most people might not even notice at first. The details make these costumes so special. It’s not just any giant hand: It’s my giant hand!” Klum said.

Heidi Klum 2026 Halloween costume, as seen from the back.

This is the 25th annual Halloween party thrown by the former Victoria’s Secret Angel: The event began in 2000, and has only continued to expand in scope. “ “Can you believe it? Twenty-five years of Halloween, costumes, incredible transformations, and so many amazing memories,” she said.

Last night’s “amputated hand” joins Klum's collection of Halloween costumes that ranges from last year’s mythological Medusa (with a petrified Kaulitz by her side) to E.T., to Shrek’s Fiona, to a disgusting giant worm inside which she feared she might suffocate. We're already looking forward to what she comes up with for next year.

#3635. Buying GTA 6 Could Save You $5,000, Or At Least This Guy Thinks So

Self-made millionaire Mark Tilbury has shared some advice for how buying GTA 6 can actually save you $5,000. Just don't take this too seriously.

Here's how he arrived at that number: If the game costs $100 (for the Ultimate Edition) and it takes 80 hours to complete, that works out to $1.25/hour of "fun." After adding on side missions and simply exploring GTA 6's map, investing in the game seems like an even better deal at just 50 cents of fun per hour.

If you play for four hours every evening, that's 50 nights of entertainment. Tilbury said people should compare this to a night out where they could easily spend $100 in a night.

"That's why buying GTA 6 actually saves you $5,000," Tilbury says.

Even if it's not a full $100, Tilbury is spot-on that going out to do most things today costs a pretty penny. So staying in to play GTA 6 may indeed "save" you some money you might have spent elsewhere. You may also play a lot of GTA 6 and continue to go out and spend money on other things.

His math also might be conservative, as people are no doubt going to play GTA 6 for far more than 50 days, especially when GTA Online 2.0 releases in 2027, as expected.

Clearly, though, Tilbury is being cheeky here and created the clip for virality and for people to send to their friends and partners to justify how much they are going to play GTA 6.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and a PC edition is expected to be released in 2027.

#3633. GTA 6 Preloading: Start Date And What To Know About Digital And Physical Copies

After years of development and multiple delays, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally launching on November 19, and you can now actually preorder the game. The $80 game arrives on November 19, but you can actually preload it a week earlier, which is nice for the countless people who no doubt want to begin playing the second they can.

Here's everything you need to know about GTA 6 preloading.

GTA 6 preload schedule

GTA 6 players who preorder a digital copy of GTA 6 can begin preloading on Tuesday, November 10 at midnight local time in your respective time zone. This is to "ensure they are able to play at launch," Rockstar said, adding that code-in-box versions for both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles should be available from retailers starting November 12.

The game's physical edition will be available to buy on November 12 "to support preloading," Rockstar said. So if you walk into a GameStop or Walmart on November 12 and see a copy of GTA 6 on the shelves to buy, you can do so, but the game itself won't unlock until November 19.

GTA 6 file size

GTA 6 is going to be massive, as Rockstar has confirmed the game will require up to 212GB of storage capacity, depending on your device.

GTA 6 launch times

#3632. One Popular PC Game Storefront Has Had Enough Of AI Slop, And It’s Taking Action

Indie game storefront Itch.io has announced it removed "a couple terabytes of AI slop" and has begun taking steps to combat the deluge of AI-created games appearing on the platform. "Just because you can upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI-generated models doesn't mean you should upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI-generated models," Itch wrote in a social media post.

The platform had already noted that the number of game pages being created per day had doubled from 3,000 to 6,000 over the last two months, with reports of users flooding the game uploads page with dozens of AI-created game spams. Going forward, Itch says that these sorts of bulk uploads will result in that spam being de-indexed, and filtering for generative AI disclosure will be added more sections of the site, including the search results page.

This doesn't mean Itch is outright banning AI-generated content, but it is taking a harder line against people who spam the site with it. In its official terms and conditions, Itch states that if the use of AI in a game is "clearly stated" and if "it adds substantial value" to the user experience, then that's okay. But if you're uploading something iterative, that'll be against the platform's rules.

Essentially, if you don't want to see AI-built games when you search Itch, the new filter will keep them out of your search results. This is a far stronger response than Valve's, as Steam's approach to AI slop has been very hands-off so far. While Valve has vaguely suggested it's considering how to address the influx of AI spam following the disastrous October edition of Next Fest, its response to developers fearful of AI-cloned projects has left much to be desired.

According to several developers, AI slop is a much bigger problem than Steam realizes.

Valve said that developers should focus on building a community and more unique features into their games to help stand out, which does nothing to address the issue of their projects being cloned the second they share progress online--although one of the big drivers behind cloned games, Anthropic's Claude, may have had its copycat abilities throttled recently.

#3631. Why Your Smartwatch Size Really Does Matter

“Is my watch too big?” is a constant question on forums dedicated to smartwatches and fitness trackers of all kinds. (Some, but fewer, wonder if their watch is too small.) Personally, I don’t much care how a watch looks, but I’ve noticed that size can make a big difference in how accurately a watch functions. If your watch is too big, your numbers may be off.

Watches measure heart rate through an optical sensor on the back of the watch. (That’s what you see glowing green back there.) The heart rate sensor detects how that light reflects off the blood vessels in your skin. To get a proper reading, it needs to be snug against your skin, ideally in a way that blocks out ambient light.

If the sensor loses contact with your skin, or if too much light sneaks in, heart rate readings may be inaccurate. If a watch fits you well to start with, you can generally get an accurate heart rate by simply making sure the watch is snug during workouts.

But if a watch is too big, it can move around, letting light in. When you run, if a watch is bouncing around, the sensor may detect a flash of light with every footstep. This can lead to your watch reporting a heart rate that is the same as your cadence (footsteps per minute), which is sometimes called “cadence lock.” Some runners will cover their watch with a sleeve (especially in cold weather) to minimize this possibility.

No matter how you wear it, a big watch on a small wrist is likely to have a lot more difficulty than one that fits properly. Very small devices can have a similar problem: The device isn’t large enough or can’t be tightened enough to block light. This isn’t usually a problem with wristwatches, but it may explain why smart rings tend to be so poor at daytime heart rate tracking.

Now, is this a real-life concern, or just a theoretical quibble? I wasn’t sure, until I took the Forerunner 265 and 265S for a run at the same time. These are the same watch, with the same heart rate sensor, differing only in size. You can read about my results here, but the graph tells the story pretty well: The smaller 265S (42 mm) captured my heart rate more accurately than the 265 (46 mm).

If heart rate accuracy were the only issue, I would tell you to get the smallest watch you can find. It wouldn’t even look weird; before smartwatches became popular, wristwatches were often much smaller than a person’s wrist. (Watch old movies and you’ll see some tiny watches, even on people who don’t have tiny wrists.)

But watches are big and seem to be getting bigger. A bigger screen means numbers, text, and icons are easier to read. This is great news if your vision isn’t the best anymore, or if you use the watch while exercising and want to be able to see what’s on your screen with a quick glance.

Bigger watches can provide bigger screens, but also bigger batteries and more room for other internals. This is probably at least partly why more “premium” watches come in bigger sizes. That said, it’s hard for me to distinguish when a watch is huge because it needs room to pack in its hardware features, versus when the company is making the watch bigger so it will seem fancier and thus justify a higher price.

And this brings me to something I need to rant about. Smartwatch and fitness watch companies know that watch size matters: They often offer two sizes for at least some of their models. The Apple Watch Series 12 comes in 42 or 46 millimeters, while the Garmin Forerunner 570 comes in 42 or 47 millimeters, to give a couple of examples.

But when it comes to premium models, those options often disappear. The Garmin Forerunner 970, far more feature-rich than the 570, only comes in a 47-millimeter size, matching the larger size of the 570 but without a smaller option. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 only comes in a 49-millimeter size, which is even larger than the larger size of the Series 12. I’m about to start testing a Hyrox feature that only comes on Amazfit’s Balance 3 or Balance Ultra watches; those watches are 51 and 52 millimeters, respectively. This is getting ridiculous.

As a woman reporting on tech, I can’t ignore the way gender plays into this. According to ANSUR II, a U.S. Army study, women have an average wrist size of 154 millimeters (about 6.1 inches), and men have an average wrist size of 176 mm (about 6.9 inches). My wrists are right around 6 inches, making me very average for a woman.

When companies make two sizes of watch, the smaller size usually fits the average woman’s wrist fairly well, and the larger size is a better fit for men’s wrists. This isn’t a perfect match, of course, since plenty of women may fit or prefer the larger size, and vice versa. I’m glad the companies market these as “small” and “large” or just by the numerical size.

But as a person with six-inch wrists, I can’t wear a large watch without dealing with bouncing, rubbing, and potentially inaccurate data. I’m no twig; I’m perfectly average for my half of the population. But those larger watches just aren’t going to be as accurate for me as they are for the average man. I noticed a similar phenomenon when I tested the heart rate tracking in Powerbeats Pro 2 earbuds: They barely worked for me, but did fine when I tried them on a man with larger ears.

There's also an uncomfortable intersection between this gender dynamic and the way watch companies use size as a signifier of how fancy a watch is supposed to be. While Garmin only offers the 970 in a large size (47 mm), they only offer the cheaper 70 and 170 in smaller sizes (both 43 mm). Garmin’s Venu 4 comes in both 41 and 45 millimeter sizes, but the cheaper Vivoactive 6 is only available in 42. Having a small wrist can save you money, but it still shuts you off from some of the more premium options out there.

For my work reviewing and testing watches for Lifehacker, I’ve worn smartwatches ranging from around 40 millimeters (an older Apple Watch) up to 48 millimeters (a tie between the Kospet Tank and the Amazfit T-Rex 3 Pro). I love a watch in the 40-42 millimeter range; I can tolerate one around 46 millimeters if it’s lightweight enough that it doesn’t bounce too much; and I really have a hard time with anything larger.

Those bigger watches are hard to snug up sufficiently for a workout; get them tight enough not to bounce, and they’ll feel like you’re nearly cutting off your circulation. After a long run with a big, heavy watch, I’ve sometimes gotten red, irritated spots on my wrist from the inevitable friction. You may not be able to judge how badly a watch will fit when it's still in the box, but I do have a rule of thumb for when you try it on.

To judge visually, I find it helps to put a watch on your wrist, rest your arm on a table, and look directly down at it. If the lugs of the watch extend past your wrist, it’s too big. You want the watch to fit on your wrist, not overhang the sides.

And if you prefer a watch size that isn’t going to be the most accurate for heart rate, remember that you can always pair a chest strap to a watch that supports it, or to your phone if you don’t have a compatible watch. If you prefer a larger watch for more readable text or maps, or if you want a premium feature that doesn’t come in smaller sizes, a chest strap may be the way to get the best of both worlds.

#3630. Former 5th Grade Teacher Pleads Guilty After Allegedly Having Student's Baby

A former New Jersey elementary school teacher who allegedly had a baby with a student has pleaded guilty in connection with sex acts involving the minor.

Laura Caron, of Middle Township, who used to teach fifth grade at Middle Township Elementary School, pleaded guilty on Wednesday, October 28, to second-degree endangering the welfare of a child with sexual conduct, the Cape May County Prosecutor’s Office announced in a news release.

Before her plea, Caron, 36, was previously indicted in June 2025 on charges of first-degree aggravated sexual assault, second-degree sexual assault and the child endangerment offense she pleaded guilty to, according to prosecutors.

The indictment came after Caron was charged in January 2025 following an investigation into her alleged “sexual relationship with a male juvenile victim,” the district attorney’s office said in the news release.

Caron was accused of an “inappropriate sexual relationship” with the student between 2016 and 2020, when the student had reportedly been living with her.

The student was 11 when Caron allegedly started assaulting him, People reported.

According to a probable cause statement viewed by the outlet, Caron had a baby girl in 2019, when the student was 13 and she was 28.

A criminal investigation ensued after the boy’s father took to social media in December 2024 and claimed Caron’s daughter looked like him and his son, per WPVI-TV.

As part of Caron’s guilty plea, she’s expected to be given five years in state prison at her sentencing, which is set for January 8, 2027, according to the district attorney’s office. She also must forfeit her teaching license and is prohibited from holding positions of public employment in the future.

Before she serves prison time, Caron will undergo an evaluation at the Adult Diagnostic and Treatment Center at Avenel, a prison and psychiatric facility run by the New Jersey Department of Corrections.

The evaluation will “determine whether she is deemed repetitive and/or compulsive which could impact her sentence,” the district attorney’s office said.

Following her sentence, she’ll be required to register as a sex offender and will be on supervised parole for the rest of her life.

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, contact the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-HOPE (4673).

#3629. GTA 6 Worldwide Release Times Revealed, And The US Gets It Almost Last

GTA 6 is one of the most-anticipated games ever, and it arrives on November 19. People naturally want to know when exactly that day it will be available to play, and now Rockstar has confirmed the details.

The game will launch at midnight local time on November 19 "in all regions" across PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Given that, it seems the US will be among the last major markets to get it.

The regional release rollout means people in New Zealand and Australia will get in first and the US will be among the final major regions to get started.

In short, GTA 6 will become available to play in New Zealand at midnight in the country, which works out to 5 AM PT / 8 AM ET on November 18. People in the US will then have to wait 16 hours to play GTA 6 where they live.

Given this, people in the US will be in for a tough day as they see the game go live for other people and have to wait. If you're concerned about spoilers, that's another reason to be on guard that day.

While GTA 6 unlocks on November 19, preloading for the 212GB game begins on November 10 for digital copies and November 12 for the code-in-a-box versions sold at retailers.

According to SensorTower, GTA 6 has already sold close to 7 million copies via preorders, and that number could climb to 25 million by launch. That would work out to more than $2 billion in revenue, which is reportedly enough to pay for the game's development budget.

#3628. The Elder Scrolls 6 Is Officially Titled Sentinel

Confirming a recent report, Bethesda has confirmed the subtitle of the next Elder Scrolls game as The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. This was shared as part of a 40-year-anniversary video recapping many of Bethesda's highlights over the year.

Unfortunately, that's all that was shared about the game, though we did get a (very familiar-looking) title card showing the game's name in the classic Elder Scrolls font. Bethesda subsequently shared a video with a scroll emerging from the sand, which you can see below.

The one hint of what might await in the game was a quote that follows the name reveal. It's attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell in 4E 206: "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Two details stick out there: the reference to a scroll and Hammerfell. A recent report from The Verge stated that Elder Scrolls VI will be set in Hammerfell and focus on the history of the titular Elder Scrolls and discovering their secrets. A follow-up tweet from Bethesda states that the game's location has been revealed, so it seems we are indeed headed to Hammerfell.

More notably, Bethesda says it'll "be some time" before more is shared, so don't expect this announcement to signal the beginning of a proper marketing campaign or anything of the sort.

The Elder Scrolls VI was announced way back in 2018, at a time that Bethesda boss Todd Howard later admitted was not his preference. Virtually nothing has been shared about the game since that debut trailer, including any imagery, hence the reason we've all seen that mountain range countless times in the eight-plus years since.

Earlier this year, it was revealed that the majority of Bethesda Game Studios staff are at work on the game, with Howard saying, “We know we need to get it right and it’s been a long time." The last core entry in the series, Skyrim, released in 2011, meaning it will be more than a 15-year gap between new games.

No release date or platforms for The Elder Scrolls VI have been announced, although Bethesda's parent company, Xbox, has faced renewed pressure to turn its business around. In part, that will involve focusing on its biggest franchises, with Fallout 5 also in the works, though Bethesda devs are said to fear further layoffs.

#3626. 10 Hacks Ever Siri AI User Should Know

Khamosh Pathak is a freelance tech journalist with over 13 years of experience writing online. An accounting graduate, he turned his interest in writing and technology into a career. He holds a specialization in user experience design from ISDI Parsons in Mumbai, where he sought to deepen his understanding of UX, consumer devices, and interplay between software and technology.

Khamosh has written thousands of how-tos and guides on every major platform (iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows). He got started writing how-tos and guides for Guiding Tech, where he also published several e-books. His work has also been seen at MakeUseOf, How-To Geek, and PCMag. He is truly passionate about brewing good coffee.

If you're like me, you've spent years ignoring most of Siri's functionality. Sure, it's great for setting timers, making calls, and sending a text. But that's kind of it—Apple's promise of an "always-on" digital assistant never truly delivered.

But that's finally changed with the recent launch of Siri AI. Fifteen years after debuting the app on the iPhone 4S and four years after the release of ChatGPT, Apple has taken the time to build out its own private Apple Foundation Models (with little help from Google) that work both on-device and on Apple's servers to give quick responses to your queries. Siri AI's answers are short, to the point, and actually useful. However, the conversational side isn't the only new thing about Siri AI. In fact, once you scratch the surface, you'll find Siri AI features embedded across the entire iOS and macOS ecosystem. Here's how to get the most out of Apple's new, enhanced digital assistant.

Siri AI is already tuned for brevity. Compared to Gemini or Claude, its responses are short and to the point. But still, if you ask something with your voice, it responds using voice as well. I personally prefer to quickly read through Siri responses. If you’re like me, you can enable a hidden setting that makes sure that Siri always answers silently, no matter if you’re writing to it or using your voice. Go to Settings > Siri > Responses and switch to the Silent Response option.

On the other hand, if you prefer to listen to Siri's responses, it's worth it to spend some time fine-tuning them. If you have an iPhone that’s under two years old, you have access to a more expressive Siri voice. Siri AI has an Expressive Voice feature that works on iPhone 17 Pro and higher, iPhone Air, and Macs with an M3 processor or higher (at least 12GB RAM).

To find this feature, go to Settings > Siri > Voice. Here, you can change the Pace to make Siri faster or slower. The big feature is the Expressivity slider; you can use it to make Siri sound brighter and more enthusiastic, rather than flat. You also have several voice options at the top (color-coded).

Visual Intelligence is deeply integrated into iOS 27 and macOS 27, and it turns anything on your screen into a source that Siri AI can act upon. It can search anything on your screen, and even take action on things it finds out. You can highlight any text on an iPhone, tap and hold, and choose the Ask Siri option. On the Mac, Ask Siri is the first option in the right-click menu. Choose a file, select text, and get started talking to Siri.

But it goes further. Just pull up Siri AI on your iPhone or Mac and start asking questions about what you’re seeing on screen. If you’re seeing a photo of a cafe on Instagram, ask where it is, or ask Siri to open it in Maps. If you’re watching a scene from a movie or a TV show, ask Siri where it’s from.

Clean Up was part of Apple Intelligence features in iOS 18, but it wasn’t great. It used on-device models to remove objects, and the results were lacking. Now that Apple runs its own Apple Foundation Models in Private Cloud Compute, it can securely process images on its servers, and the Clean Up process is much better. It now removes objects from photos very reliably, and even accounts for shadows. But to use this, you have to make sure to use the High Quality feature (instead of the default Auto mode).

Tap the Edit button in a photo, go to Tools > Clean Up, and from the top, switch to the High Quality option. Now brush over or tap an object you want to remove. Then, tap Clean Up and wait for a while until Apple’s servers complete the process. Tap Done to save the changes.

One of the most tedious parts of using the Calendar app is manually entering multiple events from a complicated schedule—say, for a season's worth of your kid’s soccer practices, or your college course's weekly lecture schedule. With Visual Intelligence in iOS 27, this is now table stakes: You can point your iPhone camera towards a schedule or take a screenshot of one, then tap the Add to Calendar button. Siri will recognize all the events, and you’ll get an option to add them to the calendar individually or all at once.

Siri AI's Mail integration is a hidden gem. Once your iPhone or Mac is done indexing your local data from Mail, you can use Siri AI to triage and manage your Mail without even opening the Mail app. In my testing, it works really well, especially because Siri AI understands the context of an email. This means you don't need to remember the exact details about the sender or the subject. You can just ask something like, "Find all emails about my flights from last week and send them to my accountant." You can also ask it to do things for you. For example, you can say, "Archive all the emails from Walmart from last month," and it will give you a one-button option to do just that.

When you start using the new Siri AI more often, you'll realize that it asks for confirmation way too often. For things like deleting mail, that's useful. But for sending messages, less so. There is a hidden setting that removes the extra step when it comes to sending messages via Siri. Go to Settings > Siri > Responses and enable Automatically Send Messages.

After the Siri AI upgrade in iOS 27, I find myself using the Camera Control often, and you should try it too. Just press and hold the Camera Control button to launch the camera's Siri mode. Point towards anything you want to find out more about and tap the big Siri icon. In a second or two, you will get the Siri response at the top, along with relevant actions based on what you're looking at. This feature is genuinely useful, and if you don't like using the Camera Control (or don't have access to it on your iPhone), you can also add the Siri AI shortcut to the lock screen, Control Center, or the Action button.

While Shortcuts has been one of Apple's most powerful features, it's also one of the hardest to use. Making an automation requires setting up steps, selecting variables, and thinking about chronology, and more. With Siri AI, Apple is trying to reduce that burden. And when it comes to simpler stuff that an everyday iPhone user needs, it works.

For example, you can open Shortcuts, create a new shortcut, and use the Describe a shortcut feature to talk about a Shortcut you want to build in natural language. You can ask Siri to create a daily morning Shortcut that shows you the day's weather, upcoming calendar events, and the to-do list for the day. You can also ask it to create a Shortcut that converts images in batches and creates new notes with a pre-made template.

While Apple is now using its own Apple Foundation Models for the new Siri AI, ChatGPT isn’t technically gone. If you have a complex question, or if Siri AI’s answer isn’t doing the trick, you can still summon ChatGPT from the Siri AI app (no need to go to the ChatGPT app for this). Tap on the text field in the Siri app, choose the Ask option and then switch to the ChatGPT service. Siri AI is quite intelligent at routing, so if ChatGPT can’t answer, it will route you back to Siri AI’s own models.

#3624. GTA 6 File Size Revealed, And It’s Truly Massive–See How It Compares To Other Huge Games

Ahead of the game's release on November 19, GTA 6's file size has been revealed, and it is massive. Rockstar Games has confirmed that people will need about 212GB of space to install the game.

As announced previously, preloading for GTA 6 begins on November 10, which is good news considering the game is massive in terms of its file size. People will no doubt have to delete other content to fit the game on the PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. This is double the file size of Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption II.

How does GTA 6 file size compare to other games?

Content creator NikTek put together a graphic that shows how GTA 6's file size, 212GB, compares to other big games--and it's the biggest.

As you can see, the next closest is Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War (175GB), followed by Assassin's Creed Valhalla (160GB), Stalker 2 (160GB), and Forza Horizon 6 (156GB).

Everyone expected GTA 6's file size to be gigantic, but now there is a number behind it, and it's one that makes it among the largest games ever in terms of file size. GTA 6's map is three times bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2's, and the game is filled with lots of detail in the vein of that game's horse testicles.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it's expected to be the biggest game of all time. One report said the game could hit 25 million preorders by launch, generating $2 billion in revenue.

GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, but it's safe to assume that Rockstar will eventually release a new version of GTA Online. A PC edition, meanwhile, is expected in early 2027.
